cases.name: Paz Véliz Soto
cases.about:
She was Salvadoran. In interview with The opinion, Albina Soto, Paz’s granddaughter, says that her grandmother had two sons, David and Eduardo, who gave her 6 children and 3 great-grandchildren. She was a widow. She lost her husband in 2013; and at 78, she was still active, working as a home caregiver.

“She was always busy, and she was friendly, chatty, vibrant.” But she also adds that she was an independent and strong woman.

“She was a loving and dedicated mother, grandmother, great-grandmother, as well as a good neighbor and friend.”
cases.narrative: On 7/16/2022, police discovered her in an alleyway with stab wounds to the upper torso.

cases.name: Judy M. Strother Taylor
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Judy had a long and illustrious career which included being one of the founding members of the Washington Free Press newspaper. She also worked at the White House Special Action Office for Drug Abuse and Prevention, provided training for federally sponsored Children of Prisoners mentoring effort and published "Training New Mentees" which has been used by thousands of mentoring programs. Judy's biggest passion in life were cats. She simply loved any and all of them. Rescued many, supplied veterinary services and worked tirelessly to find loving homes. She was the founder of Pretty Good Cat a non-profit rescue organization founded in LA and operated in both LA and La Quinta, CA."

Her work biography said: "Judy Strother Taylor has over 30 years of experience in adult and youth mentoring, human development, and juvenile justice. Judy has worked at the White House Special Action Office for Drug Abuse Prevention and she served for five years as the Project Director for the US Department of Education national mentoring initiative She also provided training for the federally sponsored Children of Prisoners mentoring effort. Judy's publication, "Training New Mentees," was originally written for the National Mentoring Center, and has been used by thousands of mentoring programs since. She recently teamed with MMS President Jerry Sherk to bring an employee-to-employee mentoring program to the US Air Force's Space and Missile Systems Center in Los Angeles, Albuquerque, and Colorado Springs."
cases.narrative: On 10/4/2023, police found her body during a welfare check. She had been shot in the head.

cases.name: Shoneka Lars
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Shoneka touched the lives of all who knew her with her caring and giving nature. 

Shoneka was truly one of a kind, a beacon of love and kindness. Her smile could light up any room, and her laughter was as contagious as her joy. She had a remarkable ability to make everyone around her feel seen and loved, and her generous spirit knew no bounds. Whether it was offering a helping hand or simply being a source of comfort, Shoneka was always there for anyone in need.

 To those who knew her, she was more than just a friend or family member—she was a literal angel on earth. Her warmth, compassion, and boundless love will forever remain in our hearts.

 Shoneka’s legacy of kindness will live on in the many lives she touched. She will be deeply missed but never forgotten."
